<reason>PRO won a competitive debate by keeping a voteable rule on the table: two people, same remaining good, same posted conditions, different stickers because software inferred who they are. CON’s inclusion story (hidden highs fund automatic lows; uniform prices exclude the poor) was the strongest opposing mechanism, but it never showed why public markdowns, inventory fares, and claimable coupons could not do that work, and the “no two checkouts share a second” move would make any ban unenforceable by design. PRO’s public-condition vs private-guess line survived pressure and made the clash easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO’s Rebuttal 2: a 15% cut is legal only as a public trigger anyone in that situation can meet; the audit is hold scarcity fixed and swap the customer. That preserved the ban’s line against CON’s incoherence and unenforceability attacks.</best_rebuttal>
